name: dusty packed wasteland earth ground, a seamless 4x4-tile field with soft clumped earth with raised clods, gentle lighter dry and darker damp areas and small grit clusters running across tile borders
label: wasteland_ruins/dirt-a

surfaces.part: packed earth ground field (seamless terrain texture, 96x80)

answer.evidence: The image is a flat terrain texture that fills the whole frame (width 96 on every row, rows 0-79). It has clumped earth, lighter and darker patches and grit specks. It has no silhouette, front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse, or vertical face. The column scans show only mottled color variation (L about 81-118) with no structural bands. As seamless ground terrain it is a top-down surface with no standing front face, which is expected for this kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 5 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Near-flat coverage is 0%, the same as both references, and the image shows no large flat areas. The earth ramp runs from light dry patches through mid brown to darker damp clods, with small grit dots, and the variation carries across tile borders, so the field reads as seamless. There are no outlines, and the 0% neutral dark edge share confirms no black sticker line; the clods are separated by value alone, as in the Beodeul references. Texture is moderate rather than rich: the clod shapes are soft and a little blobby, and the 7 total colours give fewer steps than the grass reference's clumped greens. Still, it is not thinner or flatter than the grass reference, and it matches the paving on tone count. Pass.

surfaces.part: ground texture field, full tile area, no standing object

answer.evidence: The image is a seamless terrain texture filling the full 96x80 canvas, with a constant width of 96 across rows 0-79. It has no silhouette, no front-edge line, no eave shadow, and no ellipse. The column scans show only mottled clods, light and dark patches, and grit speckles, with no structural bands. It is a flat top-down ground field, which fits a terrain kind. There is no standing object and no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a brown earth field with mottled clods, lighter dry patches, darker damp patches and small grit specks. By the measured facts it carries 5 visible tones per tile, which is above the grass reference (3) and a little below the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills, and there is no outline to speak of (0% neutral dark edges), so the look is not sticker-like. On the shading side, the ramp is only about 4-5 steps built from just 7 raw colours, against roughly 5-6 steps for the references. The clods read as soft blobs with little per-clod highlight or shadow. The grit clusters are sparse and tiny, so texture is moderate rather than rich. The tile also looks somewhat uniform and blurry next to the crisper reference grass tufts and per-stone shading. It is close, but a careful artist would likely see it as a bit softer and thinner in detail than the references. When in doubt, fail.

surfaces.part: ground terrain field, full tile, flat earth texture with clods and grit

answer.evidence: The image is a full-bleed 96-wide by 80-row seamless terrain texture. The silhouette is 96 px wide on every row, with no transparent margin and no object outline. The column scans show only mottled earth tones, with no front-edge line or eave shadow. The small dark and light patches are clods and grit scattered irregularly, not a structural edge. It is a flat ground field with no standing object, so it has no front face and reads as a flat top-down surface, which is the normal form for terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 5 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference, with 0% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the numbers do not mark it as shallow. By eye, though, it has only about 5 brown steps (7 colours in total). The clods are mostly soft blotches with little per-clod highlight or shadow, and the grit is sparse dark specks. The damp and dry patches change gradually and read as one mottled mid-brown, not as shaded raised clumps. The grass reference has distinct tufts, a lighter and darker patch and individual texture dots. The paving reference shades each stone one by one. Next to those references the candidate looks a little softer and flatter, with weak clod definition and no clear highlight ramp, so it falls short of the Beodeul bar. No outlines are used, which is acceptable for a ground tile.

surfaces.part: seamless packed earth ground field (whole 96x80 tile)

answer.evidence: This is a terrain tile, not a standing object. The silhouette is a full 96-px-wide rectangle across rows 0-79 with no outline. The column scans show mottled earth tones (L~100-109) broken by short dark patches (L~81, 3-6 rows), which are clod shadows and damp areas. They are not front-edge lines or eave shadows. There is no object silhouette, front face, edge line, ellipse, roof or container contents. It is a continuous, seamless ground texture, so the standing-object top and front rules do not apply.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a brown packed-earth field with irregular clods and darker damp patches, plus small grit specks. It measures 5 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Near-flat coverage is 0%, matching both references, so there are no flat fills. It has no outline, which suits a ground field (the tinted dark-edge share of 0% matches the grass reference). The clod shapes sit on 4-5 lightness steps and run across tile borders, so the field reads as seamless. Texture is moderate: the clods are shaded and the grit is scattered, but the raw palette is only 7 colours and the clod highlights are subtle, so it is a little less varied than the grass reference's clumps. Even so, it is not thinner or flatter than the references and a careful artist would accept it beside them.
